title: Oppositely bounded finite-free Hom commutes with termwise scalar extension
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings. Work with ordinary integer cochain complexes of modules, identified with the one-object bottom-topology module-sheaf categories [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison], and let $F$ apply $S\otimes_R-$ termwise. Let $P,N$ be $R$-complexes, with integers $a,b$ such that $P^p=0$ for $p>b$, every $P^p$ is finite free, and $N^q=0$ for $q<a$. Use the product total Hom complexes [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], equivalently the shared Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex], whose degree-$n$ differential is $d(f)=d_Nf-(-1)^nfd_P$. The normalized scalar-extension chain map [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension]
$$\chi:F\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN),\qquad (\chi(s\otimes f))_p(t\otimes x)=st\otimes f_p(x)$$
is an isomorphism of complexes, natural in cochain maps of $P,N$. More precisely, for each $n$ put $c=a-n$ and let $P_c=\sigma_{\ge c}P$ be the stupid truncation [def-kun-truncations]. Restriction of homogeneous families, with inverse inserting zero components, gives identifications
$$\operatorname{Hom}_R^n(P,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R^n(P_c,N),\qquad\operatorname{Hom}_S^n(FP,FN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S^n(FP_c,FN).$$
Under these identifications $\chi^n$ is the degree-$n$ normalized scalar comparison for the bounded finite-free complex $P_c$. Every $\chi^n$ is invertible, and its inverses commute with the Hom differentials. The truncations are used only for these degreewise identifications, with no assertion that $P_c$ represents $Q_RP$ in the derived category. No flatness of $S$ over $R$, Noetherian hypothesis, or K-flatness of $N$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of clause (3), specialized to the degree-zero scalar complex; finite-support comparison refined by degree-dependent stupid truncations.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison] to work in the punctual-site module model. At its sole object a sheaf Hom is the ordinary module of linear maps, and a product is the ordinary product, so the terms and differentials in [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] and [def-pur-hom-complex] agree. The tensor-order change $x\otimes s\leftrightarrow s\otimes x$ is well-defined by the balanced relations, and its two composites are identities. Apply [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension] to the actual scalar-extension functor $F$: its maps send $s\otimes x$ to $s\otimes u(x)$ and are additive. This supplies the chain map $\chi$ with the formula in the statement, with no boundedness or flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of (3), degree-zero scalar complex; Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes).

proof.text: Fix $n$, set $c=a-n$, and form $P_c=\sigma_{\ge c}P$ using [def-kun-truncations]. For $p<c$, $p+n<a$, hence $N^{p+n}=0$; the $p$th degree-$n$ Hom factor is therefore zero. Restriction $r_R(f)=(f_p)_{p\ge c}$ has inverse inserting the unique zero maps for $p<c$. Both composites are identities coordinatewise. The same construction gives $r_S$ after applying $F$, since $S\otimes_R0=0$: both directions of this last identification send every pure tensor to zero. Thus $r_R,r_S$ are precisely the asserted degreewise identifications. Also $P_c^p=0$ outside $[c,b]$, and every retained term is finite free; the zero terms have the empty basis. If $c>b$, $P_c=0$ and both degree-$n$ Hom modules are zero.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of (3), degree-zero scalar complex; Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes).

proof.text: For every $p$, choose a finite basis of $P_c^p$. It generates the module, as required by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Given a surjection and a map from $P_c^p$, choose a preimage of the image of each basis vector and extend linearly; this proves the lifting characterization of projectivity in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Consequently [lem-pc-finite-projective-ring-hom-extension] supplies isomorphisms $g_p:F\operatorname{Hom}_R(P_c^p,N^{p+n})\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(FP_c^p,FN^{p+n})$ with $g_p(s\otimes h)(t\otimes x)=st\otimes h(x)$. Its hypotheses impose no restriction on $N^{p+n}$ or on $S$ over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of (3), degree-zero scalar complex; Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes).

proof.text: Put $t_n=r_S\chi^nF(r_R^{-1})$. For $p\ge c$, restriction keeps the $p$th component, and zero insertion also keeps it, so $t_n(s\otimes h)_p(t\otimes x)=st\otimes h_p(x)$. For $p<c$ the source $P_c^p$ is zero and the same equation is the equality of the unique zero maps. Hence $t_n$ has the normalized coordinate formula of [lem-pc-bounded-ring-hom-extension-degree]. Apply that node to $P_c,N,n$, the interval $[\min(c,b),b]$, and the $g_p$ of Step 3. All its hypotheses hold, including when $c>b$; it requires only a module map in degree $n$. It follows that $t_n$ is invertible. The degree-$n$ map supplied by [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension] for $P_c,N$ has the same coordinates on all pure tensors. Such tensors generate, and product maps are determined by their coordinates, so that map equals $t_n$. Since $r_R,r_S$ are isomorphisms and a functor carries an inverse pair to an inverse pair, $\chi^n$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of (3), degree-zero scalar complex; Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes).

proof.text: Write $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)$ and $H'=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)$, and let $\psi^n=(\chi^n)^{-1}$. The chain equation already supplied by [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension] is $d_{H'}^n\chi^n=\chi^{n+1}F(d_H^n)$. Multiplying by $\psi^{n+1}$ on the left and $\psi^n$ on the right gives $F(d_H^n)\psi^n=\psi^{n+1}d_{H'}^n$. Thus the inverses form a chain map and both composites are the identity degreewise. This proves the complex isomorphism using the degreewise truncations only; no comparison in the derived category has been made.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of (3), degree-zero scalar complex; Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes).

proof.text: For cochain maps $\alpha:P'\to P$ and $\beta:N\to N'$, the Hom functor of [def-pur-hom-complex] sends $f$ to the family $\beta^{p+n}f_p\alpha^p$. The formula of [lem-pc-normalized-ring-hom-extension] gives, at $t\otimes x$ in coordinate $p$, both paths in its naturality square the value $st\otimes\beta^{p+n}(f_p(\alpha^p(x)))$. Equality extends by additivity from pure tensors, and then by the product coordinates to the whole degree. This proves naturality (in particular on the stated bounded classes); composing its square with the two inverse chain maps gives naturality of the inverse isomorphism as well.

source.place: Tag 0ATK (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism), proof of (3), degree-zero scalar complex; Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes).
